name: Ten stages of increasing shedding (Tattvārthasūtra 9.45)

stages.name: samyagdṛṣṭi
stages.description: Right view arisen; shedding begins to multiply.

stages.name: śrāvaka
stages.description: Right view with the small vows.

stages.name: virata
stages.description: The ascetic under the great vows.

stages.name: anantaviyojaka
stages.description: The most intense passions are removed.

stages.name: darśanamoha-kṣapaka
stages.description: View-deluding karma destroyed (destructional right view).

stages.name: upaśamaka
stages.description: Conduct-delusion being subsided (ladder of subsidence).

stages.name: upaśāntamoha
stages.description: Delusion wholly subsided (from here one falls back).

stages.name: kṣapaka
stages.description: Conduct-delusion being destroyed (ladder of destruction).

stages.name: kṣīṇamoha
stages.description: Delusion destroyed; the other destructive karmas follow.

stages.name: jina
stages.description: The omniscient conqueror; greatest shedding, leading to liberation.

notes: The Tattvārthasūtra's own ten-stage series, older than (and mappable onto) the fourteen guṇasthānas.

stages.name: adhyātma
stages.description: Study and contemplation of the realities with friendliness and the other attitudes, by one with vows.

stages.name: bhāvanā
stages.description: Daily repetition of that contemplation with a concentrated mind.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Steady, one-pointed mind on an auspicious object.

stages.name: samatā
stages.description: Seeing the agreeable and disagreeable as equal; not grasping at powers.

stages.name: vṛttisaṃkṣaya
stages.description: Cessation at the root of activity born of body and mind, yielding omniscience and liberation.

name: The five yogas of the Yogaviṃśikā

stages.name: sthāna
stages.description: Correct postures in ritual and meditation (action-yoga).

stages.name: ūrṇa
stages.description: Correct recitation of the sacred text (action-yoga).

stages.name: artha
stages.description: Attention to the meaning of what is recited (knowledge-yoga).

stages.name: ālambana
stages.description: Meditation on a support, e.g. the Jina's image (knowledge-yoga).

stages.name: anālambana
stages.description: Meditation on the formless Siddha, leading to omniscience and the cessation of all yoga.

notes: Each of the five has four grades: desire (icchā), practice (pravṛtti), steadiness (sthira), perfection (siddhi).

name: Outer self, inner self, supreme self

stages.name: bahirātman
stages.description: Taking the body and external things as oneself (commentators: guṇasthānas 1–3).

stages.name: antarātman
stages.description: Discerning the self as distinct from the body; the means (guṇasthānas 4–12).

stages.name: paramātman
stages.description: The perfected self — embodied omniscient and bodiless Siddha (13–14 and beyond).

notes: Also in Yogīndu, Hemacandra (YŚ 12) and the Adhyātma writers.

name: The four objects of meditation (piṇḍastha to rūpātīta)

stages.name: piṇḍastha
stages.description: Five visualised concentrations: earth, fire, wind, water, the essential.

stages.name: padastha
stages.description: Meditation on letters, 'arhaṃ' and the homage to the supreme beings.

stages.name: rūpastha
stages.description: Meditation on the Arhat in the assembly hall.

stages.name: rūpātīta
stages.description: Meditation on the formless Siddha until meditator and meditated are not two.

name: The eleven stages of the householder (pratimā)

stages.name: darśana
stages.description: Right view purified, with the basic qualities.

stages.name: vrata
stages.description: The twelve lay vows without transgression.

stages.name: sāmāyika
stages.description: Regular equanimity practice.

stages.name: proṣadha
stages.description: Fasting and retreat on the parvan days.

stages.name: sacitta-tyāga
stages.description: Not eating uncooked, living vegetable food.

stages.name: rātribhukti-tyāga
stages.description: (Some texts: celibacy by day.)

stages.name: brahmacarya
stages.description: Complete sexual abstinence.

stages.name: ārambha-tyāga
stages.description: Ceasing business and household undertakings.

stages.name: parigraha-tyāga
stages.description: Relinquishing property.

stages.name: anumati-tyāga
stages.description: Not giving consent to household affairs.

stages.name: uddiṣṭa-tyāga
stages.gloss: not accepting food prepared for oneself
stages.description: Living almost as a monk (Digambara kṣullaka/ailaka).

notes: Śvetāmbara list differs (view, vow, sāmāyika, pauṣadha, kāyotsarga, celibacy, living food, undertakings, employing others, prepared food, living like a monk — recalled). Stages after right view are banded B6 (cultivation after seeing).

name: The ascent through virtuous and pure meditation

stages.name: ājñā-vicaya
stages.description: Virtuous meditation on the realities as taught.

stages.name: apāya-vicaya
stages.description: Virtuous meditation on the misery of wrong ways.

stages.name: vipāka-vicaya
stages.description: Virtuous meditation on karma's fruition.

stages.name: saṃsthāna-vicaya
stages.description: Virtuous meditation on the universe.

stages.name: pṛthaktva-vitarka-savīcāra
stages.description: Scripture-based meditation shifting among aspects (stages 8–11).

stages.name: ekatva-vitarka-avīcāra
stages.description: Fixed on one aspect; destroys the destructive karmas (stage 12).

stages.name: kevala-jñāna
stages.description: Omniscience arises (stage 13).

stages.name: sūkṣmakriyā-apratipāti
stages.description: The omniscient's subtle-activity meditation at life's end.

stages.name: vyuparatakriyā-anivarti
stages.description: All activity stopped (stage 14).

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: Release from all karma; the soul rises to the summit.

notes: The living omniscient's teaching activity (stage 13) could also be read as band B8.

stages.name: gotra-yogin
stages.description: Born in a family of yogins but without the qualities; not fit for instruction.

stages.name: kula-yogin
stages.description: Born with the dharma of yogins; fit for instruction.

stages.name: pravṛttacakra-yogin
stages.description: Has the desire- and practice-grades of restraint; the teaching is chiefly for him.

stages.name: niṣpanna-yogin
stages.description: Yoga completed; beyond instruction.
